facts.text: Mat Heyden, a soldier from Fort Sherman, won a poker game that decided Hayden Lake's name, and the spelling settled as Hayden.
The Swiss‑Chalet Bozanta Tavern, designed by Spokane architect KK Cutter, lured Presidents Theodore Roosevelt and William Howard Taft to Hayden.
In 1906 investors expanded Bozanta Tavern into a resort that steamboats used to serve nearby sawmills on Lake Hayden.
The first general store and post office opened near Lake Hayden in the 1890s, later moving closer to Government Way as the town shifted from lake to road.
Hayden was officially incorporated on June 27, 1955, after a history rooted in cattle ranching, lumber, farming, and Indian folklore.
A 1936 Art Deco building on Government Way still stands today, a relic of Hayden's early 20th‑century growth.
